In this case, we use the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,⇒\,\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

 

Letting $\theta =2x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x & =\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 8\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =\int 8\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\int \operatorname{sin}⁡4x\,\text{d}x \\  & =4(-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x)+C \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
